input: Write a due diligence memo on Rippling

team.claim: Parker Conrad is co-founder/CEO; Matt MacInnis is President/CPO; Adam Swiecicki is CFO; Martin White is General Counsel; Bridget Abraham is Chief Compliance Officer. Official leadership listing as of 2026-11-09.

Forbes identifies Parker Conrad and Prasanna Sankar as co-founders in 2016. Sankar previously directed engineering at Zenefits, founded by Conrad, and served as Rippling CTO until 2020; this is historical, not a current executive role.

Albert Strasheim joined as CTO/SVP Engineering effective 2024-08-01, after leading engineering at Segment, with earlier roles at D2iQ and Cloudflare; current title requires confirmation because the present leadership-page extraction is ambiguous.

Senior departure within the review window: Adil Syed announced his exit on 2026-09-16 after seven years, describing previous CFO and global/GTM responsibilities and recent leadership of corporate development, investor relations and partnerships; self-reported.

funding.claim: Series F: $200M primary financing, Coatue lead with Greenoaks participation; transaction counsel reported an approximately $790M combined primary/common-stock transaction and $13.5B valuation on 2024-04-22. Do not treat the entire combined transaction as new company capital.

Series G announced 2025-05-09: $450M financing at $16.8B valuation, with agreements to repurchase up to $200M of employee/former-employee equity. Named investors include Elad Gil, Sands Capital, GIC, Goldman Sachs Alternatives, Baillie Gifford and Y Combinator; the announcement does not identify a lead.
Latest issuer-confirmed valuation found in opened sources: $16.8B as of 2025-05-09. Sacra says the Series G had no lead investor; this is analyst attribution, not an issuer designation.

Unconfirmed later financing: Captables, a funding-data aggregator, lists a $250M Series H dated 2026-08-06 led by Coatue. Its article explicitly relies on a financing-database entry rather than an issuer filing and gives no round valuation; require primary documents before underwriting it.

output.verdict: Rippling’s integrated workforce platform, named customers and company-claimed scale provide a credible growth thesis, supported by a substantial issuer-confirmed financing ([company announcement](https://www.rippling.com/blog/series-g-fundraising-tender-offer)). The key underwriting gaps are the quality and profitability of reported revenue, the unconfirmed later financing, and material ongoing IP/commercial litigation; proceed to deeper diligence rather than treating public growth estimates as investment-ready financials ([Sacra](https://sacra.com/c/rippling/); [court docket](https://cand.uscourts.gov/cases-e-filing/cases/325-cv-02576-crb/people-center-inc-v-deel-inc-et-al); [Runlayer complaint](https://assets.alm.com/92/6d/ccecfe98403bbd3d3c2a0fefcdbb/runlayer-complaint.pdf)).

business.claim: B2B workforce-management software unifying HR, IT and finance around shared employee data; buyers include HR, IT and finance teams. Company description as of 2026-11-09.
Modular subscription model: most products priced per employee per month; advertised starting price is $8 per employee per month plus a monthly base fee, with custom quotes. As of 2026-11-09.

Company claim as of 2026-11-04: hiring coverage in 180+ countries and device shipping to 130+ countries. These are product-coverage claims, not proof of equivalent local payroll or regulatory capabilities everywhere.
Headquarters/office footprint includes San Francisco, New York, Austin, Seattle, London, Dublin, Bengaluru, Sydney, Toronto and Singapore; company office listing as of 2026-11-09.

traction.claim: Company claim: 28,000+ companies use Rippling to manage global teams as of 2026-11-04.
Company claim: named customers include Away, Fellow, Uncommon Goods, Quince, Bombas, Sugarfina USA LLC, Simple Modern and BrewBird, as of 2026-10-23.
Company claim, reported by TechCrunch as of 2025-05-09: serves 15,000+ startups, including Cursor, Clay and Sierra; Y Combinator became a customer earlier in 2025.
Company claim: NetSuite integration synchronizes payroll, card transactions, reimbursements and bills; promoted in connection with SuiteWorld as of 2026-10-20.

red_flags.claim: Commercial/IP litigation exposure: Runlayer seeks restrictions on allegedly derived products; examine the complaint, arbitration status, indemnities and possible product-remediation costs rather than treating allegations as facts.

Bilateral Deel litigation remains active through November 2026, including counterclaims against the company and CEO; request a counsel assessment of damages, discovery burden and security-control remediation.

Reported revenue acceleration is not supported here by audited statements: the most recent revenue figure is Sacra’s estimate. Obtain revenue recognition policies, recurring-versus-pass-through revenue, retention, gross margin, cash burn and runway before underwriting.

Capitalization recency is unresolved: the reported August 2026 Series H is explicitly database-supported, with no disclosed valuation. Reconcile signed financing documents and the fully diluted cap table.

Execution/culture diligence is warranted: Glassdoor reports a declining overall rating and weaker work-life balance; validate regretted attrition, management load and implementation capacity directly.
Customer-service diligence is warranted given BBB allegations about support, billing/cancellation and onboarding; test implementation outcomes and complaint resolution through customer references.

reputation.claim: Employee-review aggregator Glassdoor as of 2026-11-09: 3.6/5 across 1,313 reviews, 66% recommend, 79% CEO approval; the site reports a 3% overall-rating decline over the preceding 12 months. Anonymous, self-selected reviews are not representative workforce research.

Glassdoor reviews dated 2026-11-06 illustrate mixed sentiment: praise for product, growth and culture alongside high deadlines and hectic pace; work-life balance is rated 3.0/5 in the snapshot accessed 2026-11-09.

Complaint aggregator BBB lists 80 complaints over the preceding three years and 35 closed in the preceding 12 months as of 2026-11-09. Published narratives allege onboarding/support, billing/cancellation and sales-promotion friction; Rippling posts responses and sometimes disputes accounts. These are complaints, not adjudicated findings or a customer-wide defect rate.

Critical legal scrutiny also concerns alleged copying of Runlayer technology, not merely Rippling’s claims against a competitor; the underlying July 2026 complaint is an adverse party account and does not establish misconduct.

missing_fields: Audited revenue, gross margin, profitability, cash balance, burn and runway as of 2026-11-09
Net revenue retention, churn, customer concentration and recurring-versus-pass-through revenue
Issuer-confirmed August 2026 Series H amount, investors, terms and valuation; current fully diluted capitalization
Current verified headcount and layoffs through 2026-11-09
Complete current executive roster, ambiguous leadership-page titles, and comprehensive senior departures since 2024-11-09
Verified regulator actions, sanctions exposure, breach scope and complete litigation inventory; no clean bill of health inferred
Current status or disposition of Runlayer arbitration and litigation beyond the opened complaint

financial_signals.claim: TechCrunch reported approximately $570M annualized revenue as of 2025-05-09, attributing it to sources speaking to The Information. This is reported-source information, not audited revenue.
Sacra analyst estimate: $1B annualized revenue in March 2026, up from $850M at end-2025, with 78% year-over-year growth. These are estimates, not company-reported or audited financial results.
TechCrunch reported cumulative financing of $1.85B and more than 4,000 employees as of 2025-05-09; these historical figures exclude any unconfirmed later financing.

Company claim: VP of HR Tahlia Spiegel said headcount grew from 1,600 to almost 5,000 over the preceding three years as of 2025-09-26 and advertised several People-team openings. This establishes historical expansion, not current headcount or absence of layoffs.

legal_and_regulatory.claim: People Center, Inc. d/b/a Rippling v. Deel, Inc., N.D. Cal. case 3:25-cv-02576-CRB, filed 2025-03-17, remains in active discovery on the court page as of 2026-11-07. The page lists Deel second amended counterclaims filed 2026-11-04 against People Center, Parker Conrad and Keith O’Brien; no merits resolution is established by this docket extract.

The 2026-02-23 dismissal order allowed core Rippling RICO/trade-secret and related theories to proceed while dismissing some claims. Survival at the pleading stage concerns legal sufficiency, not proof of espionage or liability.

Runlayer/Anysource filed a complaint dated 2026-07-28 against People Center d/b/a Rippling alleging trade-secret misappropriation, unfair competition and breach of contract during a software evaluation. It seeks emergency relief in aid of arbitration to restrict allegedly derived products; these are plaintiff allegations, not findings.
